name: Istanbul
title: Istanbul Ship Thickness Gauging | Tuzla Yards & Bosphorus
description: Ship thickness gauging in Istanbul at the Tuzla shipyards, Ambarlı and Bosphorus anchorages: pre-docking UTM, renewal survey gauging and hull structure.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement in Istanbul: Tuzla Shipyards and Bosphorus Anchorages
intro: Istanbul is both a shipowning city and a ship-repair centre. Turkish owners and managers run large fleets of bulk carriers, general cargo ships and tankers from the city, the Tuzla shipyards on the Anatolian shore of the Sea of Marmara dock and repair ships from across the Black Sea and Mediterranean, and every ship transiting the Bosphorus passes the city's anchorages. We mobilise a team from India to vessels in the Tuzla yards, at Ambarlı and at anchor, planned around docking dates and transit schedules.

highlights.p: The Tuzla shipyard zone packs many yards, floating docks and repair quays into a short stretch of coast. Renewal-survey gauging, pre-docking estimates and steel renewal checks can be programmed across several ships in one visit.

Ships waiting to transit the Bosphorus, or for orders at the anchorages off the city, sometimes lie long enough for targeted gauging, provided the work is planned around an order to proceed at short notice.
Turkish owners are active buyers of second-hand bulk carriers and general cargo ships, and many of these ships trade past their third and fourth renewal surveys on Black Sea and Mediterranean routes.

port.h: Istanbul's shipping: shipowners, the Strait and the Tuzla yards
p: Istanbul straddles the Bosphorus, the Istanbul Strait linking the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara, and through it passes a steady flow of tankers, bulk carriers, container ships and general cargo ships trading to and from Black Sea ports. Transit is governed by the Montreux Convention and managed by the Turkish Straits vessel traffic service, and larger ships, particularly loaded tankers, often wait at the anchorages at either end for their transit. The city also handles cargo in its own right: the Ambarlı terminals on the European side are the main container gateway for the Istanbul region.

Ashore, Istanbul is the centre of Turkish shipowning and ship management. Owners here have grown their fleets through second-hand purchases of Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers, general cargo ships and small tankers, and keep them trading in the Black Sea, the Mediterranean and beyond. Those ships go through their third and fourth renewal surveys under Turkish technical departments, many of which prefer to dock close to home at Tuzla where they can attend daily. Their superintendents tend to arrive at the yard with a clear idea of where a ship will need steel, and want readings that confirm or correct it quickly. Istanbul is also an active sale and purchase market, which brings pre-purchase gauging on ships changing hands between owners.

Tuzla ship repair and shipbuilding form the core of the maritime industry around Istanbul. On the Anatolian shore near the boundary with Kocaeli, the shipyard zone holds yards building chemical tankers, tugs, ferries, fishing and offshore vessels alongside repair yards with floating docks and quays. Ships from Turkish, Greek, Black Sea and other European owners dock here for renewal surveys and repairs, and a docking with steel renewal stays long enough for a full gauging programme, provided the readings are taken early enough to shape the steel order rather than trail behind it.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in and around Istanbul
p: Most structural gauging is done in the Tuzla shipyard zone, with ships in floating docks or alongside repair quays. The usual pattern is pre-docking gauging, at anchor off Tuzla or at the last cargo port, followed by in-dock gauging of bottom, side shell and tanks once the ship is dry and spaces are cleaned. Late readings hold up a yard's steel programme, so we plan the sequence with the superintendent and the yard's project manager so that measurement stays ahead of the steelwork and renewal decisions can be made area by area. Thickness measurement in Turkey's yards is as much about timing as about the readings themselves.

Outside the yards, gauging is done at the Ambarlı container and general cargo terminals during port stays, and at the anchorages off the city. Ships waiting for a Bosphorus transit can be boarded by launch for deck, hatch cover and ballast tank readings, but the plan must allow for the ship being ordered to proceed. We agree a priority list so that the most important spaces are measured first, and anything left over is picked up at the next cargo port or in dock.
list: Tuzla shipyard zone — renewal-survey and pre-docking gauging, bottom and side shell in floating docks, tanks and holds alongside the repair quays
Anchorages off Tuzla — pre-docking gauging on ships waiting for a dock, giving the yard a steel estimate before the ship arrives
Ahırkapı anchorage at the southern entrance to the Bosphorus — targeted gauging on ships waiting for transit or orders, reached by launch
Ambarlı terminals on the European side — container ships and general cargo ships gauged during port stays under terminal ISPS rules
Anchorages at the Black Sea entrance to the Strait — deck, hatch cover and ballast tank readings on ships awaiting southbound transit
Altınova shipyards in Yalova — follow-on jobs across the mouth of the Gulf of Izmit, reached by road or ferry in the same mobilisation

context.h: Port state control, the Turkish Straits and emissions rules
p: Turkey is a member of both the Black Sea MoU and the Mediterranean MoU on port state control, and ships trading between Black Sea and Marmara ports are inspected regularly. Older bulk carriers and general cargo ships on Black Sea trades attract attention for structural condition, and deficiencies found during port state control, such as wasted hatch coamings, holed ventilators and corroded air pipe heads, are often what prompts an owner to commission gauging ahead of schedule. Turkish-flagged ships and ships managed from Istanbul are classed with a range of societies, including the Turkish society alongside the larger international ones.

On emissions, the Mediterranean SOx ECA meets the Black Sea at the 41°N parallel, so the Sea of Marmara and Tuzla lie inside the ECA that took effect on 1 May 2025, while the Black Sea itself does not. Ships moving between the Black Sea and Marmara ports therefore cross the ECA boundary near the Strait, and scrubber-fitted ships docking at Tuzla offer a good opportunity to inspect wash-water and overboard piping with the hull dry. Ships trading on to EU ports also carry EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime obligations for those voyages, although Turkey itself is not in the EU.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Istanbul
jobs.p: Most Istanbul work is linked to a Tuzla docking, either as pre-docking gauging to fix the steel scope or as in-dock gauging during the renewal survey itself. The rest comes from the anchorages and terminals: ships checked between cargoes, on sale or before a charter, often with an Istanbul superintendent attending in person. The concentration of yards also makes it practical to programme several ships in one visit.
list: Pre-docking gauging on a Supramax bulk carrier at anchor off Tuzla before its fourth renewal survey, giving the yard hold frame, hopper and topside tank readings to plan steel.
In-dock gauging of bottom and side shell on a chemical tanker in a Tuzla floating dock during its third renewal survey, with cargo and ballast tanks gauged as they are certified.
Hatch cover, coaming and air pipe gauging on a general cargo ship at Ahırkapı anchorage after port state control deficiencies at a Black Sea port.
Pre-purchase gauging on a Handysize bulk carrier at anchor, with the buyer's Istanbul superintendent attending and readings reported before the sale is confirmed.
Wall-thickness readings on the wash-water and overboard lines of a scrubber-fitted container ship at an Ambarlı terminal, taken during a scheduled call on its Mediterranean and Black Sea rotation.
Magnetic particle testing of bracket toes and hatch-corner welds on an older bulk carrier in a Tuzla dock, after cracking was found at the same details on a sister ship.

logistics: The team flies into Istanbul, using Sabiha Gökçen Airport on the Anatolian side for Tuzla, which is close to the shipyard zone, or Istanbul Airport for Ambarlı and the European side. Yard entry at Tuzla, terminal passes at Ambarlı under ISPS, and launches for ships at the anchorages are arranged through the ship's agent and the yard, with crew lists and certificates sent ahead. Turkey requires visas for Indian passport holders, so we start applications as soon as the docking date is set and plan around the visa's validity if the yard slot moves.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship waiting at anchor for a Bosphorus transit?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. A ship waiting for its transit can be ordered to proceed at short notice, so we agree a priority list with the master and superintendent and measure the most important spaces first. Deck, hatch covers and ballast tanks that can be certified quickly are the usual targets. Larger scopes are better done in a yard or at a cargo port.

faqs.q: How do you work alongside a Tuzla yard during a docking?
faqs.a: We fit into the yard's programme. Before the ship arrives we agree with the superintendent and the yard which areas are measured first, so steel renewal can be decided and ordered early. During the docking we gauge spaces as they are cleaned and certified, pass readings to the superintendent as each area is finished, and mark readings on the structure where agreed so the yard's steel gangs are not left waiting.

faqs.q: Do you cover Istanbul-managed ships when they dock outside Tuzla?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Istanbul-managed ships dock at Tuzla, but some go to the Altınova yards in Yalova or to yards abroad. The scope can be agreed with the Istanbul technical department and the team mobilised from India to the docking port, subject to visas for that country.

faqs.q: Can you check air pipes, ventilators and hatch coamings after a port state control deficiency?
faqs.a: Yes. Wasted air pipe heads, ventilators and coamings are common structural deficiencies on older ships in the Black Sea and Marmara trades. We gauge the affected items and the surrounding structure so the superintendent and the attending class surveyor can decide what to renew, and we extend the scope to nearby deck plating if the readings suggest wider wastage.
